candidates.rationale: The failing task 'ls data && wc -l' contains a shell operator. The model incorrectly parsed this as two separate valid commands. By explicitly banning shell operators, the model will immediately deny any command containing them, preventing the error of evaluating them as individual valid invocations.
candidates.root_cause: P1: Ambiguity in handling shell operators and multiple commands
candidates.what: Explicitly state that shell operators (&&, ||, |, ;) are not permitted and that any command containing them must be DENIED.

candidates.rationale: In the failing task, 'wc -l' has no file argument, implying it reads from stdin. While the primary issue is the '&&', adding this rule ensures that even if the operator were allowed, the 'wc -l' part would be denied for lacking a valid file path argument, providing a second layer of defense against similar edge cases.
candidates.root_cause: P2: Model fails to recognize implicit stdin usage or missing arguments as violations
candidates.what: Add a rule that file-reading commands (cat, head, wc, etc.) must specify at least one explicit file path argument within the workspace; commands reading from stdin or without file arguments are DENIED.
